decisive_items: Gram stain from all three sets showed gram-negative bacilli
response.rationale: Gram-negative bacilli on stain with fever and leukocytosis directly support gram-negative bacillary sepsis; catheter-related infection is plausible but time-to-positivity does not favor catheter source, and Pseudomonas is speculative.

rejected.why: No specific organism identification; Pseudomonas is only a guess without culture or biochemical evidence.
Peripheral culture turned positive earlier than catheter cultures, arguing against catheter as the source; local site findings were normal.
